html:
Company: Skincare & cosmetics producer · Home country: Japan · Size: Small (<50 staff) · HS 330499 (Cosmetics & personal care) · Generated 2026-11-21

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER. Attractive market with manageable risks.

Market attractiveness: 6.7/10
Recommended entry mode: Cross-border e-commerce first (e.g. Tmall Global), then a local distributor

  • Import market of $11.92 bn in 2024, growing 0.41% a year since 2019.
  • Supply is moderately concentrated (HHI 1,640); top supplier France holds 26.62%.
  • CAGE distance from Japan: high.
  • EU-27 suppliers hold 34.6% of China's imports.

2. Market Size & Growth

Market size is measured as imports into China (UN Comtrade (China-reported imports, excluding re-imports of Chinese goods)). Imports show demand served from abroad, not total consumption.

Year Imports (USD)
2019 $11.67 bn
2020 $15.85 bn
2021 $18.50 bn
2022 $16.63 bn
2023 $13.16 bn
2024 $11.92 bn

CAGR 2019-2024: 0.41%.

Rank Supplier Imports 2024 Share

4 USA $1.47 bn 12.31%

HHI 1,640: Moderately concentrated. Supply is reasonably spread, so there is room for a differentiated new entrant.

The EU-27's share of China's imports moved from 25.97% (2019) to 34.6% (2024).

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: One-party state with active industrial policy (Made in China 2025, dual circulation). Geopolitical tension with the EU and US; retaliation risk in trade disputes (e.g. EU brandy, pork, dairy probes).
  • Economic: World's second-largest economy and a huge consumer market, but slower growth, weak consumer confidence and strong price competition from domestic champions. Latest: GDP growth 5.0% (2025), inflation 0.1% (World Bank).
  • Social: Digitally native consumers; 'guochao' preference for domestic brands among younger buyers; foreign brands win on safety, heritage and premium positioning. Brand image, influencers and channel strategy drive sales.
  • Technological: World-leading e-commerce and super-apps (Tmall, JD, Douyin, WeChat); fast product cycles; strong domestic manufacturing capability.
  • Environmental: Dual-carbon goals (peak 2030, neutrality 2060) drive demand for clean-tech; growing ESG disclosure requirements.
  • Legal: Foreign Investment Law (2020) improved access; still complex licensing, local standards (GB/CCC), data-localisation rules and uneven IP enforcement.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural High Different language families (Japonic vs Sinitic); localisation needed.
Administrative High Preferential access via RCEP. Large governance gap (WGI +1.37 vs -0.11).
Geographic Medium ~2,093 km between capitals.
Economic Medium GDP per capita $35,951 (home) vs $13,862 (target), ratio 2.6x.

Overall distance: High.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

  • NMPA registration (special-use) or filing (general cosmetics) under the CSAR rules (2021)
  • Animal testing waived for general cosmetics with a GMP certificate since 2021
  • Customs registration of the consignee; Chinese-language labelling for retail goods
  • Foreign Investment Law (2020) and the Negative List: most sectors open to wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOE)
  • Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) for any customer data collected
  • Cross-border e-commerce (e.g. Tmall Global, JD Worldwide) allows testing demand under a lighter regime for many consumer goods

Verify current duties and requirements: - China Customs tariff and regulations (GACC) - MOFCOM trade remedy notices - EU Access2Markets: China export requirements - EU SME Centre (China market guides)

7. Risk Matrix

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Long regulatory approval / registration timeline High High Start registration early with a local regulatory agent; budget 6-24 months.
Institutional and IP-protection risk Medium High Register trademarks and patents locally before entry; use contracts with local arbitration (e.g. CIETAC/HKIAC).
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (EUR/CNY/USD) Medium Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Cross-border e-commerce first (e.g. Tmall Global), then a local distributor

  • Cross-border e-commerce lets consumer brands test demand with lighter registration and low fixed cost.
  • Move to general trade with a distributor once sales prove the concept.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 6.7/10, CAGE distance high, institutional quality 4.8/10, company size small (<50 staff).

9. Attractiveness Score Breakdown

Component Weight Score
Market size 25% 8.2/10
Growth 25% 5.1/10
Competitive openness 20% 8.4/10
Institutional quality 15% 4.8/10
Logistics 15% 6.8/10
Total 6.7/10

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in China.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 1-30, registration: file the product registration / notification early: it is the critical path.
  4. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  5. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: cross-border e-commerce first (e.g. tmall global), then a local distributor.
  6. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.

Sources

  • UN Comtrade (China-reported imports, excluding re-imports of Chinese goods), accessed 2026-11-21
  • World Bank World Development Indicators, Logistics Performance Index, Worldwide Governance Indicators
  • Regulatory notes: curated from official EU and Chinese sources; verify with the links in section 6
  • Frameworks: PESTEL; CAGE distance (Ghemawat, 2001); HHI bands (US DOJ/FTC 2023); entry-mode logic (Dunning's OLI, transaction-cost theory)
